# Draft:SENTINEL (child safety software)

SENTINEL is an open-source behavioral intelligence platform for detecting child grooming on digital platforms. Released by the Sentinel Foundation in April 2026, it analyzes patterns of user behavior over time rather than scanning message content for keywords, aiming to identify grooming sequences before direct harm occurs. The system assigns a risk score between 0 and 100 to each user, accompanied by a plain-language explanation of the behavioral signals that contributed to that score.
SENTINEL is designed to assist platforms in meeting requirements under the European Union's Digital Services Act (DSA), the United Kingdom's Online Safety Act 2023 (OSA), and the United States Children's Online Privacy Protection Act (COPPA).
Background
Most online platforms use keyword filtering or reactive report-and-review systems for child safety moderation. Child grooming — the process by which an individual builds trust with a potential victim over time — frequently unfolds across multiple sessions spanning days or weeks, without any individual message necessarily containing overtly harmful content.
The Digital Services Act requires very-large online platforms to conduct risk assessments and implement mitigation measures for child safety harms. The Online Safety Act 2023 imposes similar proactive safety duties on services likely to be accessed by children in the United Kingdom.
Technical design
SENTINEL analyzes user behavior through four signal types: a linguistic signal layer monitoring conversational register shifts; a graph signal layer tracking relationship evolution and coordinated targeting; a temporal signal layer detecting escalation velocity across sessions; and a fairness gate enforcing demographic parity audits before any model deployment.
The platform comprises 13 independent microservices implemented in Python 3.12, with Node.js SDKs available.
Licensing
SENTINEL is free for non-commercial users and organizations with annual revenue below $100,000. A commercial license is required above that threshold. In 2046, the license automatically converts to the Apache License 2.0.
